note: Adapted from the original description of Sjöstedt 1911 (German, with a short Latin diagnosis), published as Eutermes bipartitus n. sp.; the alate, large and small soldiers and worker are described, from specimens taken at Mukimbungu, Congo (9 October 1904 (month 10): 3 alates, 18 soldiers, 30 workers), under rotten wood. The printed body and head lengths of the small soldier are corrupt in the scanned text and are not given; the original uses the comma as decimal separator.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldiers are of two sizes, large and small nasute soldiers: the large soldier has the head pale yellow and the nasus reddish brown, is slightly constricted behind the nasus and has the nasus very long and straight, very slightly curved above, in the same line as the frons and almost as long as the rest of the head; antennae 13-segmented. The small soldier has 12-segmented antennae, segment 3 the smallest and nearly spherical. Both soldier forms are nearest to E. clepsydra and E. coarctatus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dorsum pale reddish brown, the head darker, chestnut brown, oval, slightly narrowing forwards, densely hairy, with a yellow fontanelle spot in the middle; frons with two deep and very distinct depressions. Clypeus hardly paler than the frons, rather small, not much inflated; first mandibular tooth distinctly larger than the others; antennae (broken in the specimen) with the basal segment about as long as the following three together, but not especially thick, segment 3 very small, segments 4 and 5 equal, spherical, the outer segments becoming thicker with longer stalks. Eyes very large, round, protruding; ocelli oval, separated from the eye by less than half their diameter. Pronotum densely hairy, about 1/4 of the head width (between the eyes), transversely rectangular, the anterior margin straight, the sides first weakly and then more strongly curved, the posterior margin broadly flat and slightly concave in the middle; anterior lobe small, broadly triangular, delimited behind by a very distinct groove; posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum with a rather shallow and broad angular emargination; sternites unicolorous, the last segment of the female very large; legs unicolorous dirty yellow, densely hairy. Wings shed in the specimens seen. Body length 4 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large soldier: head pale yellow, nasus reddish brown; slightly constricted behind the nasus, the nasus area rough, the occiput smooth; nasus very long, straight, very slightly curved above, conical, in the same line as the frons, measured from the lower anterior margin of the head almost as long as the rest of the head, with short appressed pale hairs on the outside; head in posterior view transversely oval; antennae yellowish white, 13-segmented, segment 4 the smallest and slightly smaller than segment 3, segment 3 narrowing downwards into a stalk, the basal segment about as long as the following two together and narrowing downwards, segment 5 much larger than segment 4, spherical, the middle segments more spherical than the distal ones and with longer stalks, the last segment oval; pronotum about half the head width, saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe slightly narrower and shorter than the posterior lobe, the anterior margin arcuate, not concave or almost imperceptibly so in the middle. Body and legs yellowish white, the abdomen appearing dark through the dark viscera. Measurements: body length 3 mm; head length 1.33 mm; head width 0.64 mm. Small soldier: of small size, antennae 12-segmented; segment 3 the smallest and nearly spherical, the basal segment rather thick and narrowing downwards, about as long as the following two together, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3, cylindrical, slightly narrowing downwards. Measurements: head width 0.52 mm (the printed body and head lengths are incomplete in the scanned text).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale yellow, without a fontanelle spot, smooth and shining, with a few long hairs; clypeus oval, anterior margin truncate, rather large but not much inflated, concolorous with the head, bordered on each side by a brown spot; first mandibular tooth distinctly larger than the others; antennae white with a tinge of yellow, 14-segmented, segments 3 and 4 the smallest; segment 2 slightly narrowing downwards, about as thick as the basal segment; the basal segment about as long as the following two together; the outer segments slightly enlarged, the middle segments slightly narrowing downwards, the last segment oval; pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe longer, arcuate, not concave in the middle; legs rather densely hairy; tergites and sternites shining, rather densely covered with long hairs, the intersegmental membrane between them dark, rough and very finely haired. Measurements: body length 2.3 mm; head length 0.6 mm.
